payload.text: ¡Ay, qué bueno, hijo! Six P, done — it's yours. Take good care of her, she looks pretty on a full page. And listen, El Chato next to me opens for everyone at half past nine tonight; he likes people who trade straight. Now go eat something, cariño.

¡Hola, cariño! ¿Has comido ya? Mira, para empezar tu álbum te doy la Bici de Reparto por 5 P. Es una cartita bonita, de las que gustan. Y si luego quieres algo mejor, El Chato, aquí al lado, abre a las nueve y media esta noche.
Let's meet in the middle, cariño: 5 P. A little advice, cariño: a full page is worth much more than the loose cards. Swap your duplicates!
Thirty-three. Same as a minute ago. Card didn't get worse while you talked.
Buenas tardes. How very nice to see a serious face at my stall. I am after El Marqués — a Salamanca card, naturally, my favourite barrio. I offer you 61 P for it. Shall we?
Ay, hijo, qué generoso eres, pero no hace falta. La Bici de Reparto es tuya por 5 P, ni un duro más. Así empiezas tu álbum con ganas. Y come algo, que estás muy flaco, cariño.
Ay, qué simpático eres, hijo. Mira, dejémoslo en 10 P y los dos contentos, ¿eh? My late husband always said a card should go where somebody smiles at it. Take it, and go eat something warm, cariño.

¡Amigo, amigo, come close! Paco, show him — the Monumento a Alfonso XII, foil, corners perfect, straight from a collector in Madrid who cried when he sold it. Nando says only seventy-three pesetas. Seventy-three! We leave before lunch, so... sí or sí?
Nando, he's robbing us! Fine, 65 P.

Nando, he's robbing us! Fine, 56 P. Last offer, amigo! Then we are gone, eh?

Buenas tardes. How delightful — the Monumento a Alfonso XII, the jewel of El Retiro. I have waited years for that one, señor. I offer you 61 P for it.
Let us be civilised: 62 P.
You made it past Carmen. Bueno. Mercado de San Ildefonso — thirty-three. Take it or walk, no me importa.
Buenas tardes. A pleasure, truly — but no, I do not sell uncommon cards. My albums keep what they keep. Gold packs, yes, for serious people. And I buy, always. What have you brought me?
Ay, hola cariño! Come, sit a little. Have you eaten? This one here, Tienda de Discos, very pretty card — a boy traded it to me years ago, his mother still buys lettuce in that market. For you, 29 P.
I think 64 P is more appropriate.
I think 65 P is more appropriate. That is my final word on the matter.

¡Amigo, amigo! Paco here, and this is Nando — look, look, straight from the suitcase: Museo Sorolla, the light, the sea, the painter himself! Seventy-three P and it walks home with you today. Tomorrow? Tomorrow we are in another city, another plaza. ¡Setenta y tres, and you smile all week!

Twenty-two. For this card. No. Thirty-three, same as before. I do not move first.

Ay, hijo, twenty is a little thin for her. Look — 26 P, and you take her home today. That boy's mother would be happy to know she goes to someone who likes her. Eat something after, eh? You look hungry to me.

¡Ay, cuarenta y seis! Nando, hold my heart! Look, amigo — sixty-seven P, and that is us being generous because you have the face of a man with taste. Sixty-seven, the Sorolla goes in your bag, we go to the next plaza. ¡Sesenta y siete! Say sí before Paco changes his mind.

¡Cuarenta y nueve! Nando, sit down before you faint. Amigo, listen — sixty-three P. Sixty-three! Paco is cutting his own dinner for you. This Sorolla, the sea, the light... it belongs in your bag, not our suitcase. ¡Sesenta y tres! The train leaves, the price leaves with it. ¿Sí?

¡Cincuenta y dos! Amigo, escucha — they stopped printing this one yesterday, finished, no more Sorolla ever. Sixty P. Sixty, and that is our last word, no more dancing. Nando is already closing the suitcase. Say sí now, or we walk to the next plaza and you remember this forever.

Ay, cariño, you bargain like my grandson! 24 P, and we shake hands, eh? One little point, no more talk. And listen — a full page is worth much more than loose cards, so swap your duplicates. Now go eat something, hijo.
